newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish prosecutors investigate scandal crash.
newsitem.headline: Turkish prosecutors investigate scandal crash.

text.p: Turkish prosecutors have begun investigating a car crash that sparked speculation about links between the powerful state security apparatus and organised crime, the state-run Anatolian news agency said on Tuesday.

The chief prosecutor at Istanbul state security court has opened an investigation into the crash in which a gangster wanted for political killings and drug dealing died in the same car as a senior security official and a former beauty queen.

Speculation about the incident prompted parliament to call a debate on alleged state-mafia ties. The debate, scheduled for Tuesday afternoon, will be followed by a vote on holding a full-scale investigation.

Mehmet Agar resigned from his post as Interior Minister in the wake of the crash and was succeeded on Monday by Meral Aksener. An Interior Ministry statement released after her official appointment said the ministry was considering launching its own investigation.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and his deputy Tansu Ciller had both denied links between Agar's resignation and the crash.
According to media reports, Agar stayed in the same hotel as the crash victims in the Aegean resort of Kusadasi shortly before the accident.
A deputy from Ciller's True Path Party (DYP), Sedat Bucak, was also in the car when it crashed in the western town of Susurluk.
He was seriously injured and is being treated in an Istanbul hospital, where members of the well-armed Kurdish tribe which he heads were guarding him.
